reason: 'Veins not visible' means not clearly visible, read the same way as the earlier rules for 'obscure' and 'indistinct' (C174, C175). Phrases like 'achene not visible through the utricle' are relations to another part and go to pattern 09.

config/botanical_colour_synonyms.tsv already maps 'buff' to PATO:0104054 orange yellow (NARROW), and this keeps to it. PATO:0002410 beige (very pale yellowish brown) is the close alternative if the colour table is ever revised.
A crooked stem, awn or pedicel has one or more irregular angles along its length, which is the definition of PATO:0000617 bent.
An apex that narrows to a point less sharp than acute but not rounded matches the definition of FLOPO:0991096 subacute.
Leaves, flowers or perigynia that are densely arranged are crowded on the axis. This is a positional quality; PATO:0001164 dense is mass density and does not fit.

target: shoot-borne root (PO_0000042) for roots; adventitious shoot axis (PO_0025534) for shoots and sprouts
reason: 'Adventitious' names a kind of part, not a quality of it. PO has 'adventitious root' as a synonym of shoot-borne root and has a class for adventitious shoot axes; 'producing adventitious buds' is a statement that these parts are present.

'Flushed with maroon' says the part carries a faint or partial wash of the named colour over its ground colour. The colour word is the quality, and the faintness or partial cover is a qualifier kept in the RDF record (like '±', pattern 01), not a term.

target: new: colour tinge (value purple, FLOPO:0988008 / PATO_0000951)
reason: This is a faint purple wash over another ground colour. Annotate it as purple with a tinge qualifier, the same way as 'flushed'.

label: stipule-like
definition: A shape quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's similarity to the appearance of a stipule. NOTE: Sibling of FLOPO:0991200 bract-like and PATO:0002459 sepal-like.
reason: Bracts, bracteoles, sepals and leaflets are often described as resembling stipules. PATO has leaf-like and sepal-like and FLOPO has bract-like, but there is no stipule-like class.
A planar leaf, as opposed to a cylindric one, is flat, as in the earlier rule C228 for 'plane'. 'Branching in one plane' is an arrangement, not this quality.
This class already exists for stems, rhizomes and plants. Its definition is about growing along the ground and rooting at the nodes, so it fits roots only loosely.
Most examples are coloured lines ('purple lined', 'red lines along veins'), which streaked covers. A sheath that is 'longitudinally lined' with grooves would instead be PATO:0001410 striated.

target: cincinnus inflorescence (PO_0030132) or bostryx inflorescence (PO_0030134) or rhipidium inflorescence (PO_0030131) or drepanium inflorescence (PO_0030135)
reason: PO's own comment on cyme inflorescence (PO:0030126) says monochasial cymes are these four classes, each with 'monochasium' as a broad synonym. So the word names the type of inflorescence, as the union of these four.
Tridentate means having three teeth or points, and PATO:0002256 tricuspidate (having three cusps) is the existing term for that. The other option is a count of three teeth (pattern 03).
This negates 'enlarged', which the earlier rule C180 maps to PATO:0000586 increased size.

'Connective produced beyond the thecae' or 'rhachilla produced' means the part runs out beyond the apex of the structure it passes through, which is the definition of FLOPO:0991162. Fragments like 'stem: basal produced' are noise.
This is a count of seeds per fruit with an open upper bound. 'seeded' is already listed in config/flora_counted_parts.tsv, so it belongs to the count pattern.

target: brochidodromous (PATO_0001970), bearer moved from the vein to the leaf
reason: Secondary veins that loop before the margin are what makes a leaf brochidodromous. As in the earlier note on anastomosing (FLOPO:0991128), this venation quality belongs to the leaf, not the vein. The filament and phyllary examples use a different sense.
The examples mix different meanings: ring-shaped scars on bark, a ring-shaped structure at the corolla mouth, colour bands, and cells arranged in rings. No single quality fits them all.
Carunculate seeds are seeds that bear a caruncle, which has its own PO class. The 'callus' examples are a different, non-seed sense.
The definition of FLOPO:0991175 already includes flowers borne on older, leafless branches, which is what ramiflory is.
A narrowly rounded apex ends gradually in a rounded tip, which is the definition of PATO:0001950 blunt. There is no PATO or FLOPO term for 'rounded' as an apex shape.
Unspotted means not spotted, so it negates PATO:0000333.
The word means either 'frequent' (turions common), which is about how often, or 'shared' (common rachis, common involucre), which is about structure. Neither is a quality of the part.
This is pubescent with a degree word. The playbook drops such modifiers ('longitudinally fissured' becomes fissured); 'sparsely' can be kept as a degree cue in the RDF record.

label: flagelliform
definition: A shape quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's being long, slender and flexible, tapering like a whip lash. NOTE: Sibling of FLOPO:0991038 virgate (straight, stiff, wand-like); PATO:0104351 filiform is thread-like and not flexible-tapering.
reason: Long whip-like stems, branches and spadix appendages are a standard botanical character. Neither filiform nor virgate captures the long, flexible, tapering whip shape.
Apical pores, anthers or inflorescences sit at the end of the structure that bears them. 'Apical or subapical' pairs naturally with PATO:0002475 subterminal.
In floras, 'massive' means large and bulky. Increased size is the safest general reading; the word adds no shape information.

Aggregate spikes or pseudobulbs are clustered, which is PATO:0001629 aggregated (exact synonym clustered). 'Aggregate fruit' is a part, not a quality: it should go to the bearer PO:0025628 aggregate fruit.

target: docs/annotation-context-patterns.md (continuum between two values: scalloped PATO_0001889 to serrated PATO_0001206)
reason: This is a compound of two existing values joined by a hyphen. The playbook reads such compounds as a continuum between the two words, so no new term is needed.
